newsitem.title: UK: British government loses vote on education.
newsitem.headline: British government loses vote on education.

text.p: Britain's Conservative government was defeated in the House of Commons on Monday when members of parliament voted by a majority of one against a change to a bill on education.
The ruling party was defeated by 273 votes to 272.

The main opposition Labour Party said its victory over an amendment to the Education Bill showed how hard it would be for Prime Minister John Major to continue to hold power until May 1, his preferred date for a general election.
Labour deputy leader John Prescott said: "The government is in complete disarray. The prime minister talks about carrying on until May, yet it is clear that their grip on power is slipping.
"We will continue to pile the pressure on the government because the country needs and deserves a general election as soon as possible."
Labour is well ahead of the Conservatives in opinion polls. Major, whose party can muster exactly the same number of MPs as the combined opposition, must call an election by May 22 at the latest.
The issue involved in Monday's vote was not of a kind that would prompt a vote of confidence, which could push the government out of power if the Conservatives lost.
But it proves how difficult Labour can make it for the Conservatives to keep the upper hand in the House of Commons.
